chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), that he said:
Every one who is unable to fulfill a vow he made, his expiation is the expiation of an oath.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a vow that cannot be fulfilled?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the fiqh of nuzr by equating the expiation for an unfulfillable vow to that of breaking an oath (kaffarat al-yamin). This ruling provides practical legal relief for believers, ensuring that the burden of a vow is not disproportionate to one's capacity, a principle consistent with the Shia emphasis on ease in religious obligations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, form Jameel Bin Salih, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Every one who is frustrated from fulfilling his vow, so his expiation is an expiation of an oath’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from abu al-Hassan Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has narrated the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whoever makes a vow and commitment to fast and then fails to do so, the expiation on him is like the Kaffarah (expiation) for an oath.’”
